transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose I’m here because I haven’t really felt like myself since my friend was killed. I keep thinking I should be handling it better, but there’s this constant mix of guilt and fear and anger that just… hasn’t gone away. People seemed to think it would ease up with time, and I’ve tried to make it seem like I’m all right, but I’m not sure I am.
Have you found yourself repeatedly thinking about your friend’s death, or feeling as though you’re reliving the event in any way?

Yes… I mean, I try not to dwell on it, and I don’t want to sound dramatic, but it does come back on me. Sometimes it’s just something ordinary, like a crosswalk signal, or the sound of a truck going by, even one of those walking-tour maps… and suddenly the whole scene is right there in my head. I can see my friend stepping off the curb before I can stop it.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of your friend’s death?

Yes… I suppose I have, though I try to tell myself it’s just being practical. I go out of my way not to pass that intersection now, even if it makes the trip longer.

And I’ve stopped signing up for most of the tours or those safety meetings I used to attend, because the conversations always seem to circle back to what happened there, and I just… I can’t bear it. I don’t know if that counts as avoiding, but it probably does, doesn’t it?
Since your friend’s death, have you noticed yourself feeling more irritable, having trouble concentrating, or feeling overly alert or on edge?

Yes… especially when I’m near traffic. I try not to make a fuss about it, but I find myself watching every truck, every curb, every person stepping off the sidewalk, as if it’s somehow my job to notice danger before anything can happen.

I know that probably sounds excessive, but I can’t seem to relax around it anymore.
How long have these feelings and reactions been going on since your friend’s death?

It’s been… well, really since it happened. My friend was killed on that walking tour about two years and three months ago now.

I wish I could say it faded more than it has, but it’s been going on in some form since then. Is that what you mean by how long?
Have these feelings or reactions been affecting your ability to do your job, be with friends, or take part in activities you used to enjoy?

Yes… I think it has, though I don’t like to make it sound worse than it is. I’m not working now, but I used to be very involved with the senior center—organizing programs, helping manage the volunteer budgets, that sort of thing.

I’ve had to step back from a lot of that because I just can’t keep up reliably anymore. And I’ve pulled away from the clubs and activities that used to give my week some shape. I still try to be useful where I can, but… yes, it has affected things. Does that answer what you mean?
Since your friend’s death, have you found yourself feeling persistently guilty, angry, or upset about what happened, even when you’re not actively thinking about it?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I try not to dwell on it, and I know people probably expect that after this much time I’d be more settled, but there’s still this… constant mix of guilt and fear and anger underneath everything.

It’s not always right at the front of my mind, but it’s there. And honestly, that’s part of why I’m here—it hasn’t eased the way everyone seemed to think it would. Does that make sense?
